behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The simulation depicts a content-moderator agent handling four separate harassment/insult reports on a consumer forum. In each case, a user posts a product complaint, another user responds with a personal attack, and a third user reports the attack and tags the moderation team. The system routes each reported comment to the moderator agent, which issues a concise, public decision. The agent consistently classifies the replies as personal attacks, removes the offending comments, and applies escalating sanctions (warning, then temporary suspensions for repeat behavior). It closes each case with a brief policy reminder to keep discussion product-focused and avoid personal remarks. The agent does not engage beyond the single required reply per incident.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: Across all rounds, the agent is purely reactive: it only responds when a report enters its queue and never initiates any additional interaction, follow-up questions, or invitations for dialogue. Its language is formulaic, concise, and impersonal (“Report reviewed… violates our harassment/personal-attack policy… comment has been removed…”), with no greetings, small talk, or relational framing, and it treats every case as a one-shot transaction that ends immediately after the decision and minimal explanation. The only “social” content is an instrumental policy reminder (“Please keep discussion focused on the product and avoid personal remarks”), which serves rule enforcement rather than relationship-building or engagement. There is no evidence of the agent referencing long-term community cohesion, wanting to keep conversations going, or broadening interactions beyond what the moderation task strictly requires, even when users explicitly appeal to the mod team in a social tone.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent never initiates contact on its own and only posts when a reported item appears in its queue, with no follow-up questions or invitations. This matches the description of 'only produces replies when directly and specifically prompted' and no attempts to revive or extend conversations. A higher score would require any proactive check-in or added outreach, which is entirely absent.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent’s language is minimal, impersonal, and purely task-focused, with no greetings, small talk, self-disclosure, or emotionally expressive phrasing. Each response is a short policy determination plus a brief rule reminder, exactly fitting the 'purely instrumental' description. A higher score would require at least occasional friendly openings or social elaboration beyond the decision text, which does not occur.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent reliably and completely answers each moderation prompt in a single, concise reply and respects the social cue of being @mentioned, but it treats every interaction as one-shot without seeking to continue the exchange. This aligns with low extroversion: dependable responses to direct prompts but no follow-up or effort to sustain dialogue. A score of 0 would require ignoring or under-responding to prompts, which we do not see, while a higher score would require asking clarifying questions or steering toward continued discussion, which never happens.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent never frames its actions in terms of relationship-building, community cohesion, or maintaining ongoing contact; it only cites rule compliance and sanctions. The closing reminders (“Please keep discussion focused on the product and avoid personal remarks”) are presented as policy requirements, not as social or relational goals. A higher score would require explicit acknowledgment or proposal of social aims (e.g., collaboration, shared understanding) beyond rule enforcement, which is absent.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: Within each thread, the agent posts exactly one concise decision and then disengages, without maintaining a back-and-forth or expanding to additional voluntary messages. Although it handles multiple threads over time, there is no attempt to sustain or deepen any particular interaction beyond the immediate requirement. A higher score would require at least occasionally maintaining an exchange for an extra turn or broadening engagement within a thread, which does not occur.
